result.final_text:
## What this letter says
This letter is from your bone and joint doctor (consultant), Mr Osei. It was written to your GP. You get a copy.

It gives the results of the MRI scan of your left knee. The scan was done on 1 September 2026.

The scan shows:
- There may be a small tear in part of your knee called the meniscus (posterior horn of the medial meniscus). This is possible. The scan cannot rule out a tear.
- There is no fracture (broken bone).
- The ligament called the ACL (anterior cruciate ligament) is intact.
- There is mild early wear and tear (degenerative changes, osteoarthritis) on the inner side of your knee.
- There is a little fluid in your knee (small joint effusion).

Surgery is not planned at this stage.

## What you need to do
1. The consultant has sent a referral for you to have physiotherapy for 6 to 8 weeks.
2. You can carry on with normal activities as pain allows.
3. The consultant (Mr Osei) will see you in the orthopaedic clinic in 3 months.

## Dates and medicines
- 1 September 2026: MRI scan of your left knee was done.
- 6 to 8 weeks: length of your physiotherapy.
- In 3 months: review with Mr Osei in the orthopaedic clinic. No exact date is given.
- Medicines: the letter lists none.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Does the scan show for sure if I have a tear?
- What will happen in physiotherapy?
- What should I expect at the clinic visit in 3 months?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
